observation: The 'never downloads a document' claim is not fully enforced. On a listing target whose HEAD showed no document content type (including an empty content type), the runner GETs and writes the whole body (up to 3 MB) to disk before classifying it from the first 8 bytes, and deletes it afterwards. A server that answers HEAD and GET differently, or omits Content-Type on HEAD, can therefore deliver up to 3 MB of document bytes. The log would show this (DOCUMENT_PAYLOAD/UNKNOWN fails validation), but the transfer would already have happened. The PDF signature check also misses leading bytes before %PDF. No such event appears in D_requests_v2.tsv: every non-robots GET is METADATA_OR_LISTING.
evidence: run_guarded_discovery.py curl(...max_bytes=3_000_000) and the GET branch; discovery_guard.classify_response
recommended_resolution: Before more use: refuse GET when HEAD Content-Type is empty, or stream with a small cap (Range 0-1023 / --max-filesize ~64 KB) and abort on a signature or document type. Search the first 1 KB for the signature. Change the docstring to say what is actually enforced. Add a mocked-curl test of the runner.
